entries.sentence: The NHS lists burning when passing urine, needing to go more often or more urgently, and cloudy or bloody urine as common signs.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Lower tummy pain or back pain can happen, and fever, tiredness and weakness can also appear.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: NIDDK, a US health institute, describes similar bladder infection symptoms, including discomfort in the lower abdomen and strong-smelling urine.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: When a bladder infection spreads to the kidneys, NIDDK lists fever and chills, nausea or vomiting, and pain in the back, side or groin.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Age changes the picture.
entries.note: Framing sentence; supported by M and MC excerpts below.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus says confusion or other mental changes may be the only sign of a kidney infection in older people.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Young children may have a fever, a poor appetite or vomiting, or sometimes no symptoms at all, according to MedlinePlus.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Older children may have cloudy or strong-smelling urine, or start wetting again after being toilet trained.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus says bladder infection symptoms most often go away within one to two days of starting treatment, while kidney infections can take a week or longer.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: According to MedlinePlus, a health professional can usually tell whether someone has a UTI from a urine test.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: A urine culture, where a urine sample is grown in a laboratory, can identify the bacteria and help choose the most suitable antibiotic.
entries.note: Culture identifies bacteria/helps select antibiotic per MedlinePlus; the 'grown in a laboratory' explanation is a plain-words gloss.

entries.sentence: NIDDK says that sometimes a diagnosis cannot be confirmed from symptoms and test results, and antibiotics may then not be needed.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: A Danish audit of general practice found that nearly half of patients with lower urinary tract symptoms were given antibiotics even though a urine dipstick test was inconclusive.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: In children, doctors weigh the child's age and any earlier UTIs when deciding on follow-up tests.
entries.note: Search summary attributed this to guideline-style text; likely MedlinePlus children page but summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: One review says repeated UTIs, especially in people with dementia, should prompt imaging to look for kidney stones.
entries.note: Case report and literature review.

entries.sentence: NIDDK says antibiotics are the usual treatment for bladder infections, and the length of treatment depends on how severe the infection is and whether symptoms settle.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: The NHS says antibiotics are not always needed.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: A GP may suggest self-care with painkillers, a short course of antibiotics, or a delayed prescription.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Drinking more fluids can ease symptoms and help recovery, according to NIDDK.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: NIDDK also stresses finishing the whole antibiotic course, because antibiotic resistance could make a later infection harder to treat.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Most people with a kidney infection are treated at home with antibiotics and sometimes painkillers, the NHS says.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Antibiotics through a drip in hospital are generally for more vulnerable people, such as those who are pregnant or have long-term conditions.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: NHS advice generally favours paracetamol for pain and fever in a kidney infection and cautions against ibuprofen, which may affect kidney function.
entries.note: Search summary said 'Several NHS sources'; not tied to a single page.

entries.sentence: NHS Scotland says UTIs in children can usually be treated at home with antibiotics if the child is over three months old and not at risk of serious illness.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus notes that surgery may be needed if repeated infections are caused by a problem with the structure of the urinary tract.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: One review defines recurrent UTI as two or more infections in six months, or three or more within a year.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: The same review says about a quarter to a third of adults have another infection within a year of the first.
entries.note: Summary: 'About 25-30%'.

entries.sentence: Anything that stops the bladder emptying fully, such as kidney or bladder stones or medical devices, raises the risk in both men and women.
entries.note: Summary of recurrent-UTI search; attributed to the review, not confirmed per page.

entries.sentence: Prevention options discussed include a single antibiotic dose after sex, or a short course kept at home to start when symptoms begin.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: NIDDK says vaginal oestrogen increases good bacteria and helps prevent infection.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: One systematic review, however, found no clear benefit from any currently available intervention for preventing recurrence.
entries.note: Summary says 'one systematic review'; page not individually confirmed.

entries.sentence: An NHS England campaign for older adults, who made up almost three fifths of UTI admissions over five years, recommends staying hydrated and washing regularly.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus names kidney infection, sepsis and premature delivery as the main complications.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Sepsis is a dangerous whole-body reaction to infection.
entries.note: Plain-words definition.

entries.sentence: The NHS says a kidney infection can be serious if untreated because it can cause sepsis.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: A review adds that undiagnosed or poorly managed infections can lead to chronic infection, urosepsis or kidney damage.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: For care, the NHS says confusion, drowsiness or trouble speaking with a suspected UTI means calling 999 or going to A&E.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Older adults, people with diabetes, catheter users and pregnant women are advised to get an urgent GP appointment or call NHS 111.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: For a kidney infection, NHS advice is an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111 for a very high or very low temperature, lower tummy or back pain, blood in the urine, or passing no urine all day.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: NI Direct says to see a GP if symptoms are very uncomfortable or last more than five days.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus says symptoms that return soon after antibiotics also need prompt contact with a health professional.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: The NHS says antibiotics are not always needed, and a GP may offer self-care with painkillers or a delayed prescription.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: A Gloucestershire NHS leaflet suggests that drinking more water at the first sign of symptoms can sometimes be enough.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: The same leaflet says that if symptoms do not improve within 48 hours, a GP or NHS 111 should be contacted.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: NIDDK says a bladder infection can spread to one or both kidneys.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Kidney infection signs include fever and chills, nausea or vomiting, and pain in the back, side or groin.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus says kidney infections can take a week or longer to clear, longer than most bladder infections.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: The NHS says a kidney infection needs urgent attention because it can cause sepsis.
entries.note: K says kidney infection can be serious if untreated as it can cause sepsis; 'urgent attention' is per urgent-GP/111 advice.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus says young children may have a fever, poor appetite or vomiting, or no symptoms at all.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Older children may have blood in the urine, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, or wetting problems after toilet training.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus says UTIs in children should be treated quickly with antibiotics.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: A child under six months old, or with other complications, should see a specialist right away.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Confusion, drowsiness or trouble speaking needs 999 or A&E.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: One review says an abnormal urinary system raises the risk of recurrence.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Conditions that stop the bladder emptying fully, such as stones or medical devices, also raise the risk in men and women.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: Because stones can be behind repeated infections, one review says recurrent UTIs should prompt imaging in some people.
entries.note: Search summary of this page/excerpt states this; summaries blend pages.

entries.sentence: A GP may discuss long-term low-dose antibiotics or referral to a specialist, the NHS says.
